page.layout: One column of verse, centred on the page, with the running head above it and the page number at the top right. No notes in the margins.

main_text.p: Seruauit Ascher littora fluctibus Adesa raucis, & propinquis Tunc pelago requiuit oris?
Dicenda pubis laus Zabulonia, Lugente fortis pro patria mori Virtus per orbem viuet vsque: Nephthalidumq; decus peremne.
Nam non pauente te funera pectore Hostem sequuti per inga montium Duris fatigarunt ruinis, Atque truces domuere turmas.
O, quàm feroci vidimus impetu Funesta Martis prælia feruidi Reges Chananaos inure[?]!
Quàm rapidis properare bigis Tabnaci[?] ad agros, non procul vuida Lymphis Meguiddä[?]! Sed simul hostium Hîc omnis occisa est iuuentus Et validi cecidere reges.
Hîc militarunt gentibus Abrami Commota cœlo sydera, & igneum Hîc æther aduersas cecidit Grandine lethifero cateruas.
Hîc texit austo[?] reflunt[?] aluneo Kiscon Sisarä penitus agmina.
Hîc robur hostilesque turbas Examines pede lata pressi[?].
Nonne hîc, tenaci quum celeres luto

page.notes: Woodcut-style initial N in "Nonne" and in "Nephthalidumq;" is read as N. The ligatures in "Ascher" and "Sisarä" are read as printed. Several words are doubtful because of the ink and the scan: "inure" (line 14), "Tabnaci" (line 16), "Meguiddä" (line 17), "austo" and "reflunt" (line 24), and "pressi" (line 27). A faint mark in the right margin beside line 8 is not text and is left out. Stains and show-through from the reverse are not transcribed. The page ends mid-poem at line 28, with no catchword or signature visible.
